data.title: Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 Futures Jump Nearly 2% After Brutal Tech Selloff Last Week: GME, JNJ, ALNY, GAP In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • The Nasdaq Composite fell 10% last week, while the S&P 500 and Dow fell more than 8% each. 
  • Some market participants believe that the AI selloff is overblown and that the current dip represents a buying opportunity. 
  • JPMorgan analysts said in a note over the weekend that the firm remains confident in the durability of the AI supercycle, supported by lower leverage and improved positioning. 

U.S. stock futures staged a sharp rebound and turned green late Sunday as they look to recover from one of Wall Street’s toughest weeks, which saw a sharp selloff in technology and AI-related stocks.

As of 9:32 p.m. EST, Dow futures climbed 1.54%, while the S&P 500 futures gained 1.96% and Nasdaq-100 futures increased 2.33%.

On Friday, the three U.S. benchmark indexes closed significantly lower amid rising concerns about the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite led the decline, shedding more than 1,200 points to close 5.28% lower. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 1.93% lower and the S&P 500 fell 3.70%.

IndexMoveClose
Dow Jones Industrial Average-1.93%48,147.33
S&P 500-3.70%6,910.39
Nasdaq Composite-5.28%22,617.73

Markets were a bloodbath last week amid the tech-led selloff. The Nasdaq Composite fell 10%, while the S&P 500 and Dow fell more than 8% each.

U.S. President Donald Trump said in a post on Truth Social that he “predicted” that if the Democrats win the midterm elections, the stock markets would go down substantially.

Tech Rout Weighs Heavily On Markets, But Some See Opportunity In The Dip

Last week, technology and AI-related stocks saw a massive drawdown amid rising concerns over artificial intelligence’s sustainability.

Recent upheaval in Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) leadership, rising inflation concerns and the potential of a rate hike in the Federal Reserve’s upcoming December policy meeting pressured markets.

Trump blamed Democrats for the sharp decline in markets, saying in a Truth Social post, “The Market is down more than 6 Trillion Dollars since the Democrats’ rather strange ‘win’ on November 3rd. NASDAQ, by itself, is down 20%. This is 100% due to the fact that the Democrats are ‘BAD’ due to their Anti Growth, and Retribution Only, Policies, and worse. If they don't change, FAST, it will only get worse.”

Meanwhile, some market participants believe that the AI selloff is overblown and that the current dip represents a buying opportunity.

Fundstrat's Tom Lee said in a recent CNBC interview that the recent sell-off is a healthy reset rather than a sign that the AI boom is at its end.

While acknowledging that the past few weeks have been "tumultuous" for tech stocks and the market, with investors grappling with doubts about AI spending, financing structures and the sustainability of lofty valuations, he said that he sees this to be a "pretty healthy correction in tech and it's along the narratives to reset."

He drew comparisons with how Cisco fell nearly 50% over three months in 1997, only to rebound the following year.

"I think that we are at that moment where it feels like max pain, but for the patient investor, this is going to have a big payoff," Lee said. "I don't think that this means it's the end of the AI trade," he said, adding that AI would remain "one of the biggest stories" next year.

Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster also noted that the latest sell-off in the market is more a fear-based move than deteriorating fundamentals. In a note last week, Munster said that while investors may be getting caught up in worries about what could go wrong, they are missing the picture on what AI could ultimately deliver.

He cautioned against drawing a conclusion that the AI market is in a bubble from the price action alone, noting that the Nasdaq's roughly 16% decline since the start of October was not unprecedented. He compared it with the approximately 24% sell-off during the early-2025 DeepSeek shock and tariff uncertainty.

"At its core, this sell-off is not about fundamentals, it's about psychology," he said, adding that, "The unfortunate answer is that the sell-off will end when [we] have more buyers than sellers."

Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives called the AI sell-off one of the most "disconnected" downturns that he has seen in his career, saying that stocks are pricing in the possibility that the AI revolution simply goes away. "I believe we are less than 15% through" the AI opportunity, he said, calling it "a generational opportunity to buy the winners."

JPMorgan analysts said in a note over the weekend that it is reiterating its view that the recent pullback in risk assets is mostly an AI de-leveraging event amidst weak sentiment, coupled with a more hawkish Fed reaction function being priced in. “We keep the faith in the durability of the AI supercycle, supported by lower leverage and improved positioning,” it said, according to Bloomberg.

Markets will be watching for developments in the AI trade in the holiday-shortened week with Thanksgiving on Friday.

Iran Uncertainty Lingers Amid Rising Tensions In The Strait Of Hormuz

Meanwhile, on the geopolitical front, the uncertainty around the conflict between the U.S. and Iran sent long-term Treasury yields higher and exerted added pressure on market sentiment.

Trump said over the weekend in an interview with Fox News that he may be inclined to order military strikes against Iran after the new year if an agreement does not come to fruition. He also dismissed the ongoing diplomatic talks with Tehran as meaningless, and accused negotiators of the country of stalling.

The president also said that while he wants a "permanent" deal with Iran, he added that Iran doesn’t “want to make a deal that's acceptable to me.”

Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said as per a Reuters report that the country wants a diplomatic resolution to the ongoing war and confirmed that talks with the U.S. were ongoing through mediators.

Araghchi added that Iran was seeking an agreement with the U.S. that would ensure that there would be “no further war,” according to the report.

"I believe a fair solution can be reached ​on the issue of ​nuclear material, one ⁠that is based on our national interests while also meeting the country’s needs," he reportedly said.

Brett Erickson, Managing Principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors said in a post on X, “Wanting something, and actually being able to accomplish it are two very different things, and this is greatest problem for the United States against Iran. President Trump and his ‘advisors’ may desperately WANT to change the outcome of this war, but they very simply do not have a course of action to do so. Sometimes you just have to take the L whether you like it or not.”

However, oil prices continue to cool amid a supply increase. The International Energy Agency has forecast a roughly 2 million-barrel-a-day surplus this quarter.

Brent crude futures were trading at $92.23 a barrel, down 0.37% at the time of writing, while WTI crude futures traded 0.24% lower at $83.21 per barrel.

Trump said in a post on Truth Social, “Isn’t it interesting that Oil prices have dropped precipitously after the Midterm Elections? I said that was going to happen. The whole thing is a Giant Hoax!”

Gold, Silver Extend Selloff 

Meanwhile, the precious metals trade continued to plunge sharply, with gold spot prices steadily declining. Spot gold closed down 8.71% this week at $3,543.60, down about 37% since its record high of $5,589.38 on Jan. 28. Silver also dropped sharply and is now about 65% below its January high, according to TradingView data.

Rising Treasury yields and expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December weighed on precious metals.

Trending Tickers To Watch 

GameStop Corp. (GME): The entertainment company was on the retail radar following Keith Gill’s return to social media activity where he posted a mysterious image of "Cat Mario" from Super Mario 3D World, inciting anticipation around a market-moving announcement.

Johnson & Johnson (JNJ): The company garnered attention amid recent speculation of its potential acquisition of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) after it recently acquired privately held biotech company Ollin Biosciences for up to $3.4 billion.

Alnylam Pharmaceuticals Inc. (ALNY): Retail sentiment around the stock improved from ‘bearish’ to ‘neutral’ over 24 hours as the stock edged higher overnight following a slump of nearly 3% on Friday.

Gap, Inc. (GAP): Shares of the clothing retailer edged higher in the overnight session after jumping nearly 12% at close on Friday following its strong third-quarter earnings results.

Other Market Trends 

Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) was up nearly 2% in the overnight session at the time of writing, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) gained 2.4% and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged 1.5% higher.

The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was trading at 4.95%, while the 30-year yield was at 5.337%.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was down 0.18% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment.

Asian markets opened lower on Monday. South Korea's KOSPI, China’s SSE Composite index, Japan’s Nikkei 225 and Australian stocks all traded in the red at the open.

data.title: SBI chairman warns AI errors could spread across India's banks
data.description:
Mistakes made by artificial intelligence could ripple through linked systems and expose financial institutions to serious governance risks, State Bank of India Chairman C S Setty said at an event in Mumbai, Business Standard reported on November 19.

The warning from the head of India's largest lender comes as banks hand more work to autonomous systems. Setty said lenders needed clearly defined permissions, transaction caps, audit trails and ways for humans to step in. He noted that the Reserve Bank of India's AI policy places final responsibility for governing the technology on bank boards.

He said AI brought considerable productivity benefits but also created fresh governance dangers. Institutions had to know exactly what such systems were allowed to access, which decisions they could take and when a person must intervene, he said.

Boards should ensure AI is adopted to serve the institution's purpose rather than because of technological momentum, Setty said. The tools should meet real business needs, such as better customer service, sharper risk management or wider access to finance. He cautioned that AI must not inadvertently shut out rural borrowers, small firms or people without conventional credit records.

According to him, no other bank in the system had put a responsible AI policy in place before SBI, and that policy defines the principles and limits governing how AI is used throughout the organisation as well as who is accountable for it. Directors, he said, had to be able to evaluate algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, data governance and model risk. Boards already go through yearly cybersecurity drills, and he suggested that learning about AI be built in next to those exercises.

Setty said an institution unable to explain why an AI-driven process refused a loan, flagged a transaction or triggered an action would face serious governance problems. AI worked best where parameters could be set and relevant data existed, he said. Crises and unfamiliar strategic choices still required a board's collective judgement.

Setty said fraud risk management and business operations are the main areas where the bank applies AI and machine learning. One of its patented models assesses roughly 23,000 branches and places each in a very high, high, medium or low risk band, which helps the bank determine the order in which branches are audited.

data.title: Kuwait offers more December naphtha on FOB basis, document shows
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) has offered 50,000 metric tons of full-range naphtha via a tender on a free-on-board (FOB) basis from its ports, a document reviewed by Reuters showed on Monday.

The cargo is set to load between December 7 and 8 from Kuwaiti ports, the tender - which closes on November 24 - showed.

The state-owned refiner last sold 50,000 tons of full-range naphtha for loading between December 3 and 4 on an FOB basis at a low-double-digit discount to Middle East quotes.

KPC has sold several cargoes on an FOB basis this month mostly at discounts, after previously selling naphtha on a delivered ex-ship (DES) basis at premiums amid disruptions to trade flows through the Strait of Hormuz, market participants said.

Oil companies typically do not comment on tenders.

data.title: Kogan.com Lifts Early-Year Earnings as Mighty Ape Turns Positive
data.description:
Kogan.com Limited has lifted group adjusted earnings by almost 50% in the first four months of its new financial year, as its Australian retail business grew and Mighty Ape returned to positive operating earnings.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 49.4% to $15.2 million between July and October 2026, against group revenue growth of just 3.5% to $161.5m.

For the four-month period, the Australian business produced gross profit of $65.3m, an 18.1% increase that outstripped its revenue growth as its gross margin improved to 46.4%.

The group’s adjusted EBITDA margin reached 9.4%, up from 6.5% a year earlier, reflecting improved gross margins and a smaller cost base at its New Zealand operation.

Kogan.com is meanwhile stepping up marketing for its Kogan FIRST membership program ahead of peak trading, accepting a near-term constraint on margins to build recurring revenue.

Growth Beneath the Headline

While Kogan.com’s Australian business increased revenue 12.2% to $140.6m, its adjusted EBITDA rose 13% to $15m, with its margin holding at 10.7% despite heavier marketing spending.

That spending is directed towards Kogan FIRST and the holiday trading period, with gross sales growth accelerating during the first 20 days of November compared with the July-to-October pace.

“Our marketing investment impacts profitability in the short term, but builds a larger Kogan FIRST membership base, supporting recurring revenues and future earnings growth,” founder and chief executive officer Ruslan Kogan said.

“This is a deliberate investment in our long-term growth.”

Mighty Ape Finds Firmer Ground

At Mighty Ape, the shift away from unprofitable product categories continued to weigh on sales, which fell 31.7% to $20.9m in the July-to-October period.

Yet the New Zealand retailer achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.1m, compared with a loss in the previous comparable period, while gross margin climbed 8.7 percentage points to 33.7%.

The recovery followed a difficult 2026 financial year in which Mighty Ape’s revenue declined 30% to $85.6m and its full-year adjusted EBITDA deteriorated to a $3.3m loss.

By the final quarter of that year it had returned to positive quarterly adjusted EBITDA of $0.4m after reducing inventory from about $21m to $10m and cutting quarterly fixed costs by 30.8%.

Longer-Term Strategy

The change in mix is central to Kogan’s longer-term strategy, which favours membership income, marketplace fees, service commissions, and advertising over inventory-heavy product sales.

Across the 2026 financial year, group gross sales surpassed $1 billion and adjusted EBITDA increased 13.8% to $41.8m, supported by stronger trading and profitability at Kogan.com.

Free cash flow rose 18.2% to $38.3m, leaving $36.4m of cash and no debt after the group returned $34.9m to shareholders through dividends and share buy-backs.

For the medium term, management continues to target a group adjusted EBITDA margin of 8% to 12%, with the latest 9.4% reading placing it within that range while investment in Kogan FIRST continues.

data.title: Mike McGlone Says Crypto Crash Is A Preview Of The 'Everything Bubble' Bursting, Sees Bitcoin At $10,000 Again
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bloomberg's McGlone said most tokens like Dogecoin will probably drop to roughly zero.
  • He said that Bitcoin's summer rally gave fake hope that kept the bear market going.
  • He also sees crude oil falling back toward $40 and copper dropping below $5.

Crypto's slump is just the first sign of a much bigger market bust, says Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodity strategist Mike McGlone.

In a post on X on Sunday, McGlone said the Bitcoin and crypto bear market that started in October 2025 could show what is coming for most other assets. He named U.S. stocks, gold, metals, commodities, and Treasury yields. "Bear markets can take money from everyone," he wrote. "It's simply overdue reversion."

Why BTC Can Fall To $10,000

McGlone stuck to his long-held belief that Bitcoin will fall to $10,000. He called that level a "good gravity-pull pivot." He said an asset with unlimited supply shouldn't be expected to outperform other assets. This isn't a new call. McGlone has said Bitcoin could fall to $10,000 since at least April 2025.

Bitcoin's price rose more than 1% over the past 24 hours, trading at $60,765 at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the 'bullish' zone, while chatter around it stayed at 'high' levels over the past day.

Warns Dogecoin Could Go To Zero

His prediction was harsher for the rest of the market. Most tokens that are tracking nothing, like Dogecoin (DOGE), will probably drop to about zero, McGlone said. He compared crypto to non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and the Dutch tulip mania. From 1634 to 1637, prices of rare tulip bulbs soared and then collapsed from extreme highs.

He also mentioned Strategy (MSTR), the biggest corporate Bitcoin holder. "MSTR is likely to get stopped out," he wrote.

Bitcoin's summer rally is a trap, McGlone said. The coin rose from around $58,000 in June to nearly $86,000 in September. More sharp short-covering rallies like that are likely across markets, he said. He calls them "false hope" that extends the bear market.

Pain Beyond Crypto: Stocks And Commodities Are Next

The pain will extend far beyond crypto, McGlone said. He's looking for a 50% drawdown that likely started at the Oct. 6 high. Now, he expects the S&P 500 Total Return index to end 2026 lower for only the third time since 2009. He said that gold, silver, copper, natural gas and the Nasdaq have made big gains this year and could now unwind.

Other calls he makes include crude oil falling back to $40 and copper dropping below $5. "US housing has peaked along with inflation," he said, adding that "this is a normal cycle of post-inflation deflation."

When Feds Will Step In

McGlone also sees the Fed starting to ease. That puts him at odds with recent market action. According to CME Watchtool data, 93.5% of the markets expect a rate hike in the upcoming December policy meeting.

"The gift of 2026 for investors" is Treasury yields at near three-decade highs, he said.

McGlone cited one thing that would disprove him. U.S. stocks would need to stay near their highest levels relative to GDP in a century or so. "The trading year of a lifetime is more likely to end like a lion than a lamb," he wrote.

McGlone’s call comes at a time when along with Bitcoin, gold and silver has also been under pressure, with Goldman Sachs seeing the possibility of $80.6 billion sell-off in stocks this week.

data.title: Tata Power targets 6.8-GW pumped hydro storage pipeline in India
data.description:
Tata Power plans to grow its pumped hydro storage portfolio to 6.8 gigawatts (GW) through two new projects, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director Praveer Sinha told Moneycontrol in an interview.

The utility is pushing deeper into energy storage while also widening its presence in renewable power and transmission. India is heading into another year of strong growth in electricity consumption and new generating capacity, and storage allows power from intermittent sources such as solar and wind to be held back for use when demand peaks.

The company already has two pumped hydro schemes in development, at Bhivpuri and Shirwata. The two further projects would take the pipeline to 6.8 GW.

Sinha said Tata Power also sees business opportunities in battery storage for homes.

The company intends to keep capital expenditure at INR250bn ($2.7bn) in FY28, the financial year ending in March 2028, according to Sinha.

He added that curtailment of renewable energy, when available green power cannot be fed into the grid, could ease considerably from the July to September quarter of FY28. New transmission lines are expected to start operating by then.

data.title: South Korea's finance minister sees solid growth next year, flags chip volatility risks
data.description:
By Yena Park and Cynthia Kim

South Korea's economy is expected to sustain a solid growth trajectory next year as robust exports and investment gradually spill over into domestic demand, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said on Monday.

Speaking ahead of a news conference in Sejong, Lee said Asia's fourth-largest economy is currently maintaining strong momentum and could achieve growth in the upper-3% range if present trends continue.

He added that consumer inflation is projected to ease next year compared with this year, supported by stabilizing global oil prices, though both upside and downside risks remain.

Despite the upbeat baseline outlook, Lee warned that external risks remain severe, citing regulatory uncertainty surrounding the artificial intelligence industry, geopolitical instability and rising global interest rates. He cautioned that volatility in the semiconductor sector could spill over and amplify broader macroeconomic swings.
